notes: Handheld supercardioid condenser vocal microphone capsule (d:facto II series, "Softboost" variant with +3dB boost at 12kHz; the 4018VL "Linear" variant is otherwise identical). Modular design: the wired configuration reviewed here uses the standard DPA Handle terminating in a male XLR-3 (XLR-3M) output carrying the balanced audio signal and receiving 48V (±4V) phantom power over the same connector, per DPA's published mic wiring convention (pin 1 shield, pin 2 signal+phase, pin 3 signal-phase) — consistent across DPA's condenser mic line. The same capsule is also sold with wireless-transmitter adapters (SE2/SE5 for Sennheiser, SL1 for Shure/Sony/Audio-Technica/Lectrosonics/Wisycom, WI2 for Wisycom) instead of the XLR handle; those variants have no user-facing connector at all (the capsule mates to a proprietary transmitter body) and are out of scope for this single-port XLR entry. No other physical ports exist — it is a passive-powered (phantom) single-connector microphone with no separate power inlet, no controls, no data ports.
